The current implementation of `expand_tabs` seems to be:
1. It creates a `blank_copy` of `self`.
2. It iterates over lines and parts split by `\t`.
3. If a part ends with `\t`, it replaces the `\t` with a space and appends the part.

Summary of fix:
Modified `rich/text.py` in the `expand_tabs` method to ensure that when tab characters are expanded into spaces, the generated spaces preserve the style of the tab character instead of falling back to the default style of the `Text` object. This was achieved by using `part[len(part)-1].style` to retrieve the style of the tab character.

The bug in `rich/text.py` was that the `expand_tabs` method used the default style of the `Text` object (`self.style`) for all spaces generated during tab expansion, regardless of the style applied to the tab character itself.

I have fixed this by modifying the `expand_tabs` method to retrieve the style of the tab character (which is the last character of the current text segment `part`) and applying that style to the expanded spaces.

```python
# Before
if spaces:
    append(" " * spaces, _style)
    pos += spaces

# After
if spaces:
    append(" " * spaces, part[len(part)-1].style)
    pos += spaces
```

This ensures that the styling of tab characters is correctly preserved when they are expanded into spaces.
